To block Brave, X and Telegram, PBlock needs to run as an accessibility service.

1. Press “Open settings”.
2. Find “PBlock protection” under “Installed apps” / “Downloaded apps”.
3. Turn it on and allow it.

If the switch is greyed out (“Restricted setting”): Settings › Apps › PBlock › ⋮ menu › “Allow restricted settings”, then try again.

PBlock collects and sends no data: it only watches which app is in the foreground.

This makes the system automatically restore the DNS filter after a reboot or a crash.

1. Press “VPN settings”.
2. Tap the gear next to PBlock.
3. Turn on “Always-on VPN”.

Important: do NOT turn on “Block connections without VPN”! PBlock only routes DNS traffic through the VPN, so that option would cut off all other internet traffic.
As a device admin, PBlock prevents itself from being uninstalled during the challenge. It requests no other permissions.

A custom Private DNS provider is set on the phone (%1$s). In that case the system can send DNS queries encrypted, bypassing PBlock, so the filtering is not reliable.\n\nChange it: Settings › Network & internet › Private DNS › “Automatic” or “Off”.

• Chrome: Settings › Privacy and security › “Use secure DNS” → turn it OFF, otherwise Chrome can bypass the filter.
• Firefox, Edge, Opera and other browsers: turn off “DNS over HTTPS” / “Secure DNS” and any built-in VPN.
• Private DNS: Settings › Network & internet › Private DNS should be “Automatic” or “Off”.
• Besides the blocklist, the filter also uses Cloudflare’s family DNS (1.1.1.3), which screens out further adult sites.

Pause for a minute and a half. An urge is like a wave: it rises, peaks and passes. Breathe with the circle.

string-array.name: hard_moment_messages
string-array.item: An urge is a wave. It rises, peaks and fades, usually within 15–20 minutes. You don\'t have to do anything with it.
You\'ve done hard things before. This is one more of them, and it\'s smaller than it feels right now.
Nothing has to be decided in the next ten minutes. Just get through these ten.
Feeling the pull doesn\'t mean you\'re failing. Noticing it and pausing is exactly the skill you\'re building.
Tomorrow morning\'s you will be glad about what you do right now.
Boredom, stress, loneliness or tiredness: which one is really knocking? Give that one what it needs.
Your brain is asking for a quick reward. A glass of water, a short walk or a message to a friend counts too.
Every day you get through makes the next one a little easier. That\'s how habits change.
You set up this challenge on a calm day for a reason. Trust that version of you.
It\'s okay that this is hard. Hard doesn\'t mean impossible.
Put the phone down for a moment, stand up and look out the window. Let this moment pass.
You are not your urges. You\'re the one who chooses what happens next.
Count what you\'ve already gained: time, focus, energy. Don\'t trade it for a few minutes.
Slow down. Unclench your jaw, drop your shoulders and take one more slow breath.
Even if yesterday was rough, today is a fresh start. You\'re here, and that counts.

string-array.name: hard_moment_actions
string-array.item: Go for a 10-minute walk, even just around the block.
Splash cold water on your face or take a cool shower.
Do 20 push-ups or squats right now.
Slowly drink a big glass of water.
Message or call a friend, about anything at all.
Leave the room and do something with your hands for 10 minutes.
